title: Initial ridge-spur settlement working landscape
scope: Qualitative local-crown placement, unequal-shoulder managed apron, near-settlement land-cover sequence, lake-road relationship, and layered water access and storage for Project Hearthway's initial ridge-spur settlement; usable within shared-setting location, geography, ecology, culture, logistics, and story development without establishing exact infrastructure, hydrogeology, reliability, society, or events.
claims: The fortified core occupies the local crown of the ridge spur already established by WLD-ECOLOGY-004.
An unequal-shoulder managed apron surrounds the local crown.
The innermost part of the managed apron is a deliberately maintained low-vegetation warning belt.
Beyond the warning belt, small and incomplete contour terraces occupy some usable steeper upper slopes.
Broader fields and grazing ground occupy the gentler lower shoulder.
Woodland resumes beyond the managed apron and comes closer to the fortified core on steep or otherwise difficult sides.
A constructed road descends in bends toward a lake that lies beyond the immediate managed apron but within regular local travel and haulage reach.
A spring emerges within the fortified perimeter and is incorporated into settlement water access; wells supplement that access, and cisterns provide stored water.
boundaries: This record is a forward local implementation of WLD-ECOLOGY-004's fortified ridge-spur core within WLD-GEOGRAPHY-001's initial-region scaffold; it does not alter the principal lower-basin crown-herd corridor, lake, regional drainage, climate, coast, or wider basin arrangement.
